title: Aura Skills
description: Aura skills. @aura/skill-aura and procedure skills install to .agents/skills/.

files.content:
# Aura CLI

Run commands with the project package runner. This repo uses pnpm.

```bash
pnpm dlx @aura-design/cli@latest init
pnpm dlx @aura-design/cli@latest setup
pnpm dlx @aura-design/cli@latest blueprint
```

`init` scaffolds a Next.js app, Aura tokens, and the blueprint. `setup` applies Aura to an existing Next.js app. `blueprint` writes the feature map, the always-on process rules, and the forms stack under `.agents/`.

Registry items:

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @aura/skill-aura
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @aura/rules @aura/skills @aura/rule-design-md
```

`@aura/skill-aura` installs this directory to `.agents/skills/aura/`. `@aura/rules` installs the always-on process rules to `.agents/rules/`. `@aura/skills` installs procedure skills to `.agents/skills/`.

Consumers can also install this skill, once the repo is the source the skills CLI reads, with:

```bash
pnpm dlx skills add somosgented/aura-design-system --skill aura
```

Token commands (`colors`, `spacing`, `typography`) write theme output. Read `DESIGN.md` before changing a scale by hand. Do not invent flags that are not in the command `--help`.

# Customization

`DESIGN.md` is the narrative spec. Change tokens there and in the theme CSS the CLI writes. Do not add a parallel palette in a component.

## Map shadcn semantics onto Aura

| shadcn example | Aura |
| --- | --- |
| `bg-background` | `bg-gray-1` or `bg-gray-2` |
| `bg-primary` | `bg-accent-9` (`--primary` maps to `--accent-9`) |
| `text-primary-foreground` | `text-accent-contrast` |
| `text-muted-foreground` | `text-gray-11` |
| `border-border` | `border-gray-6` |

## Add a color

Ask for an accent or gray seed and run `aura colors`, or extend the existing 12-step scales in the theme file. A one-off hex on a component is not a theme.

## Add a component variant

Appearance changes belong on the component (`variant`, `size`), then a story. Call sites keep layout and width.

# Color Step tables live in `DESIGN.md` §2. Use the steps; do not paste the tables here. ## Contents - Accent and gray steps - Role by step - Contrast - No raw palette --- ## Accent and gray steps **Incorrect:** ```tsx
Panel
``` **Correct:** ```tsx
Panel
``` Use `--accent-{1–12}`, `--gray-{1–12}`, and alpha `--accent-a*` / `--gray-a*`. Prefer semantic tokens (`--primary`, `--accent-surface`, `--accent-contrast`) when the theme already maps them. --- ## Role by step | Steps | Role | | --- | --- | | 1–2 | Backgrounds | | 3–5 | Interactive fills | | 6–8 | Borders and focus | | 9–10 | Solid brand | | 11–12 | Text | **Incorrect:** ```tsx

Body on a gray page

Card
``` **Correct:** ```tsx

Body on a gray page

Card
``` Map `--primary` to `--accent-9`. On a transparent control, hover may use step 3. --- ## Contrast Steps 11 and 12 must meet APCA Lc 60 and Lc 90 on step 2 backgrounds. Do not lighten text or darken the canvas to make a marketing sample fit. --- ## No raw palette One-off hex and Tailwind palette utilities (`bg-pink-500`, `text-emerald-600`) are not the production source of truth. Status color goes through a semantic token or a component variant.

# Forms

Applies when editing forms (`**/form.tsx`, `**/Form.tsx`, `**/use-dynamic-form.ts`), server actions (`**/actions.ts`, `**/Actions.ts`, `**/*-actions.ts`, `**/*Actions.ts`, `app/**/route.ts`), and validation schemas (`**/validation/**`, `**/Validation/**`, `**/*schema*`, `**/*Schema*`). The end-to-end procedure is skill `aura-forms`.

Forms use **useFormDynamic** for state, **Form** for error distribution, and **validateFormData** from `@/utils/web-validation`. Schema property names match field names so errors match by `instancePath`.

## Contents

- ajv, not another validator
- Shared schema and server action
- Field components and the 17px floor

---

## ajv, not another validator

Validate with ajv via `validateFormData` / JSON Schema; do not add zod, yup or valibot.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

const profileSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email(),
});
```

**Correct:**

```ts
const profileSchema = {
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    email: { type: "string", format: "email" },
  },
  required: ["email"],
  additionalProperties: false,
};
```

---

## Shared schema and server action

Keep each JSON Schema in one shared module (for example `lib/validation/<name>.schema.ts`). The client form and the server action import the same schema.

Build forms with `useFormDynamic(initialValues, formRef?)` and pass fields from `getFields()` / `field(name)` into Form field components. Validate with `validateFormData(schema, formData.getValues())` and pass returned `errors` to `<Form>`. On failure call `formData.touchForm()`.

Submit to a Next.js server action. Inside every action, check auth and authorization, then re-validate the input with `validateFormData` and the shared schema. Return `{ errors }` in the ajv shape so `<Form>` can show them.

**Incorrect:**

```tsx
<input aria-invalid={Boolean(errors.email)} />
```

**Correct:**

```tsx
<Form errors={errors}>
  <FormField field={email} label="Email">
    <Input type="email" />
  </FormField>
</Form>
```

Do not pass `errors` into each field. Use `FormField`, `FormSwitch`, `FormCheckbox`, and groups per control type. Use `FormAlert` when `fetchStatus === "error"`.

---

## Field components and the 17px floor

Keep editable controls ≥ 17px (see [typography.md](./typography.md)). Do not override control padding via call-site `className`.

# Icons Default library is `@radix-ui/react-icons`. Prefer one library. If a second is required, Radix plus that one. ## Contents - className="icon" - Gap, not margin - Button and Badge --- ## className="icon" **Incorrect:** ```tsx import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from "@radix-ui/react-icons"; ``` **Correct:** ```tsx import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from "@radix-ui/react-icons"; ``` Never pass `size`, `width`, or `height`. Size through typography: `icon`, `icon h4`, `icon h1`. Ignore shadcn `data-icon` and Lucide defaults unless the installed component API requires them. --- ## Gap, not margin Space an icon from its label with the container `gap`. A row that only holds the icon and label uses `gap-0.5`. **Incorrect:** ```tsx
Search
``` **Correct:** ```tsx
Search
``` `aura/no-icon-margin` forbids `ml-*`, `mr-*`, `mx-*`, `ms-*`, and `me-*` on the icon. `ml-auto` and `mr-auto` are allowed only to push layout. --- ## Button and Badge Those controls already own gap. Do not add an icon gap class inside them. **Incorrect:** ```tsx ``` **Correct:** ```tsx ```

# Lint

`@shadcn/lint` is the machine-checkable layer for Aura Tailwind policy. `DESIGN.md` and this skill say what to do. Lint says how to fix the file. Install, ESLint merge, and the post-UI fix loop live in skill `verify-aura-ui`.

## Contents

- After UI edits
- What the rules catch
- Call-site className

---

## After UI edits

Run the project `lint` script (`pnpm lint`) and clear `@shadcn/lint` findings you introduced. Prefer zero new `shadcn/no-restyle` and `shadcn/no-arbitrary-values` on touched files.

| Rule | Catches |
| --- | --- |
| `shadcn/no-arbitrary-values` | Values off the 13px scale |
| `shadcn/no-raw-colors` | Raw palette instead of tokens |
| `shadcn/no-restyle` | Restyling design-system components via `className` |
| `aura/no-icon-margin` | Horizontal margin on icons inside gap-owning controls |

---

## Call-site className

**Incorrect:**

```tsx
<Button className="bg-pink-500 px-[16px] text-sm">
  <MagnifyingGlassIcon className="icon mr-2" />
  Save
</Button>
<Input className="px-3 text-xs" />
```

**Correct:**

```tsx
<Button>
  <MagnifyingGlassIcon className="icon" />
  Save
</Button>
<Input className="w-full" />
```

Prefer theme tokens (`accent-*`, `gray-*`, semantic) and the 13px scale. Do not restyle a design-system component with padding, color, or typography via `className`. Use variants and sizes, or layout and width only.

`Input`, `Textarea`, `SelectTrigger`, `MaskInput`, and `SegmentedInput` own their padding. Never put `text-sm` or `text-xs` on an editable control. Never add horizontal margin to an icon inside `Button` or `Badge`.

# Product principles

These constrain product and UX choices. Visual tokens stay in `DESIGN.md` and the other files in this folder.

## Accessibility

Products must be usable by any user. Build for perception and operability.

**Incorrect:** an icon-only button with no accessible name, or a control that only works with a pointer.

**Correct:** a visible label or `aria-label`, a focus ring, and keyboard operation.

## Consistency

Teams share one objective and one voice with the user, visual and written.

**Incorrect:** one screen says “Delete”, the next says “Remove forever”, with a different button variant.

**Correct:** the same verb, the same variant, and the same confirmation pattern.

## Reusable

An hour spent on a component should prevent someone else from rebuilding it.

**Incorrect:** a second date field with its own markup because the first one was hard to call.

**Correct:** one field component, called twice.

## Shareable

Build with tools that let the team share the work.

**Incorrect:** a local-only snippet that never lands in the registry or the story.

**Correct:** a registry component and a story the next person can install.

## User control

The user must feel in control of the product.

**Incorrect:** a flow that submits on a timer or hides the way back.

**Correct:** an explicit submit and a way to leave.

## Forgiveness

The user must be able to change their mind or repeat a process.

**Incorrect:** a destructive action with no undo and no way to start again.

**Correct:** confirm, then undo or a clear retry.

## Perception of stability

Even on complex platforms, processes should feel simple and familiar.

**Incorrect:** a new layout and a new vocabulary on every step of one task.

**Correct:** the same shell, the same terms, one decision at a time.

# Spacing `--spacing` is **13px**. Before any `m` / `p` / `gap` / `h` / `w` / `size` utility, compute `unit * 13px`. `p-4` is 52px. Detail in `DESIGN.md`. ## Contents - Half-unit scale - Pixel requests - Containers --- ## Half-unit scale Use 0.5-unit increments only (`1`, `1.5`, `2`, …). **Incorrect:** ```tsx
``` **Correct:** ```tsx
``` `gap-*` over `space-y-*`. For a vertical stack: `flex flex-col gap-*`. --- ## Pixel requests Convert “about 20px” to `1.5` (19.5px), not `2` (26px). **Incorrect:** ```tsx
``` **Correct:** ```tsx
``` Skip arbitrary pixel spacing unless the human explicitly asks for that pixel value. --- ## Containers Sections use a defined container (padding, margin, max-width). Prefer five container types or fewer per project.

# Ownership

`DESIGN.md` is the narrative spec. This skill is the design guardrail agents load for UI work. Process policy stays always-on so it is present even when this skill is not.

| Layer | Owns | Does not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DESIGN.md` | Narrative design (tokens, theme, product voice) | Step-by-step procedures |
| `.agents/skills/aura/` | Design guardrails and Incorrect/Correct pairs | Feature-map writes, comment policy, install recipes |
| `.agents/rules/*` | Always-on process rules: `feature-map`, `no-comments`, `design-md`, monorepo `agents-md` | Color, type, spacing, icons, motion, forms, lint |
| Other skills | Procedures (`aura-forms`, `verify-aura-ui`, `port-component-to-aura`, `update-feature-map`, `generate-brand-images`, upstream `shadcn`) | A second design policy |

Cursor reads `.agents/rules/*.mdc` directly. The `rules/*.md` files in this skill are references linked from `SKILL.md`, same as the shadcn skill. They are not a second copy of the always-on rules.

## Keep

Do not weaken these when editing the skill or a component.

- 12-step chromatic scale (`--accent-*`, `--gray-*`) with APCA contrast roles for steps 11–12 on step 2.
- Fluid typography via `clamp()` and a global **≥ 17px** floor on editable form controls.
- Strict **13px** spacing base (`unit * 13px`).
- Icons use `className="icon"` only. No horizontal icon margins inside gap-owning controls.
- The only project documentation is the feature map in `wiki/obsidian-{suffix}/Feature-Map/`, updated inside the PR that changes a feature. See `.agents/rules/feature-map.mdc`.
- No code comments except external constraints (with the reason), directives, licenses, and generated code. See `.agents/rules/no-comments.mdc`.

## Upstream shadcn skill

Installed with `pnpm dlx skills add shadcn/ui` into `.agents/skills/shadcn`. Use it for the shadcn CLI, registry search, composition discovery, and presets.

When that skill conflicts with Aura Keep, **Aura wins**:

| Topic | Prefer Aura | Use the shadcn skill for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Icons | `@radix-ui/react-icons` + `className="icon"`; no `ml-*` / `mr-*` on icons in `Button` / `Badge` | Component discovery. Ignore `data-icon` and Lucide defaults unless the installed component API requires them |
| Forms | `useFormDynamic` + `Form` / `FormField` + `validateFormData` (skill `aura-forms`), submitted to a server action that re-validates with the same shared schema. ajv via `validateFormData` / JSON Schema. Do not add zod, yup, or valibot | `FieldGroup` / `Field` only when the Aura form stack is absent |
| Spacing | 13px scale (`gap-0.5` = 6.5px, `gap-2` = 26px) | `gap-*` over `space-y-*` |
| Color | `--accent-*` / `--gray-*` and semantic tokens | No raw palette. Map shadcn semantics onto Aura tokens |
| Typography | Fluid `.h1`–`.p`. No `text-xl` on primary copy. Inputs ≥ 17px | Layout and `cn()` that do not fight the floor |
| Restyle | Variants and sizes. `@shadcn/lint` `no-restyle` | `className` for layout and width only |

**Incorrect:** a shadcn snippet copied with `data-icon`, `size-4`, and `bg-primary` left as a raw Tailwind semantic that was never mapped.

**Correct:** the same composition with `className="icon"`, Aura gap, and `bg-accent-9` or the semantic token `DESIGN.md` already maps.

Do not vendor the shadcn skill into `packages/registry` or `sync-skills.ts`. Blueprint installs shadcn and gdp-ts with `skills add`. Third-party UI, motion, and performance audits are not part of Aura. See `/docs/audits`.

## Routing

- Code comments and workarounds → `.agents/rules/no-comments.mdc`
- UI tokens → `DESIGN.md`, then this skill
- shadcn CLI, registries, presets → skill `shadcn`
- After UI edits → skill `verify-aura-ui`
- Opening or updating a PR → skill `update-feature-map`
- Porting external UI → skill `port-component-to-aura`
- Aura forms and server actions → skill `aura-forms` and [forms.md](./forms.md)
- Monorepo design-system edits → skills `aura-constraints` / `aura-verification` and root `AGENTS.md`
- Third-party audits → `/docs/audits`

# Typography Scale tables and the clamp formula live in `DESIGN.md` §3. ## Contents - Fluid primary copy - Utility text - 17px control floor --- ## Fluid primary copy **Incorrect:** ```tsx

Title

Paragraph

``` **Correct:** ```tsx

Title

Paragraph

``` Size primary type with `clamp(var(--min), var(--val), var(--max))` through `h1`–`h6`, `.h1`–`.h6`, `p`, and `.p`. `--min` and `--max` are `rem`. Large headings use line-height about 1.1–1.3. `blockquote` shares the `h4` scale. --- ## Utility text `text-sm` and `text-xs` are for fixed utility or meta text only. **Incorrect:** ```tsx

--- name: aura description: Applies the Aura Design System when building or editing UI, tokens, theme, forms, icons, motion, spacing, or Tailwind classes. Use for the 12-step accent and gray scales, the 13px spacing grid, fluid clamp typography, the 17px form-control floor, Radix icons with className="icon", @shadcn/lint, and Aura component composition. Triggers on Aura, DESIGN.md, aura init, aura setup, aura blueprint, @aura registry items, and any task that styles product UI with Aura tokens. Aura Keep invariants win over the upstream shadcn skill. user-invocable: true --- # Aura A registry-first design system. Components are copied into the app and updated with the Aura CLI and the `@aura` shadcn registry. Narrative tokens live in root `DESIGN.md`. Monorepo policy lives in root `AGENTS.md`. This skill is the design guardrail agents load when the task is UI. Always-on process rules stay outside this skill, in `.agents/rules/` (`feature-map`, `no-comments`, `design-md`, and in this monorepo `agents-md`). Cursor reads that directory directly. Do not fold them into this folder. ## Principles 1. **Tokens before one-off values.** Accent and gray steps, semantic roles, and the 13px grid. Detail in `DESIGN.md`. 2. **Compose Aura components.** Use variants and sizes. `className` is for layout and width. 3. **Keep type fluid and controls readable.** Primary copy uses the clamp scale. Editable controls stay at least 17px. 4. **Leave the user in control.** Accessible, consistent, reversible, and familiar. See [principles.md](./rules/principles.md). 5. **Aura wins over shadcn defaults.** When this skill conflicts with `.agents/skills/shadcn`, follow the table in [surface.md](./rules/surface.md). ## Critical Rules These rules are **always enforced** for Aura UI. Each file has Incorrect/Correct pairs. ### Color → [colors.md](./rules/colors.md) - **12-step `--accent-*` and `--gray-*`.** Plus alpha `--accent-a*` / `--gray-a*`. Prefer semantic tokens when they exist. - **Roles by step.** 1–2 backgrounds, 3–5 interactive fills, 6–8 borders and focus, 9–10 solid brand, 11–12 text. - **Steps 11–12 stay APCA Lc 60 / Lc 90** on step 2 backgrounds. - **No raw palette or one-off hex** as the production source of truth. ### Typography → [typography.md](./rules/typography.md) - **Primary copy uses the fluid scale.** `h1`–`h6`, `.h1`–`.h6`, `p`, `.p` — `clamp(var(--min), var(--val), var(--max))`. - **No `text-xl` / `text-2xl` / `text-4xl` on primary copy.** - **`text-sm` / `text-xs` are utility and meta only.** Never on `input`, `textarea`, or `select`. - **Editable controls stay ≥ 17px.** ### Spacing → [spacing.md](./rules/spacing.md) - **`--spacing` is 13px.** `p-4` is 52px. Only 0.5-unit increments. - **About 20px is `1.5` (19.5px).** Not `2` (26px). - **No arbitrary pixel spacing** (`p-[16px]`) unless the human explicitly asks. ### Icons → [icons.md](./rules/icons.md) - **`@radix-ui/react-icons` and `className="icon"`.** No `size`, `width`, or `height` props. - **Gap owns the space.** No horizontal margin on an icon. `Button` and `Badge` already own gap. ### Motion → [motion.md](./rules/motion.md) - **`transform` and `opacity` only.** Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`. - **CSS theme tokens.** No decorative autoplay. ### Forms → [forms.md](./rules/forms.md) - **`useFormDynamic` + `Form` + `validateFormData` (ajv).** Do not add zod, yup, or valibot. - **One shared JSON Schema.** The server action checks authz, then re-validates with that schema. - **Procedure:** skill `aura-forms`. ### Lint → [lint.md](./rules/lint.md) - **After UI edits, run `pnpm lint`.** Clear `@shadcn/lint` findings you introduced. - **Fix loop:** skill `verify-aura-ui`. ### Ownership → [surface.md](./rules/surface.md) - **`DESIGN.md` is the narrative spec.** This skill is the design guardrail. `.agents/rules/*` is process policy. - **Do not vendor** the shadcn or gdp-ts skills into the Aura registry. ## Key Patterns ```tsx

Section

Body copy uses the fluid scale.

Panel
``` The first block is the pattern: gray step 2 surface, fluid heading, `gap-2` (26px), icon class `icon` inside `Button`. The last two blocks fail: arbitrary spacing, raw color, restyled button, icon margin. ## Workflow 1. **Read `DESIGN.md`** when the task touches tokens, theme, type, spacing, or motion. Do not copy its tables into this skill. 2. **Check installed Aura components** before writing new UI. Add from the registry with the project package runner. See [cli.md](./cli.md). 3. **Apply the Critical Rules** while editing. Map shadcn examples onto Aura tokens ([customization.md](./customization.md)). 4. **Verify.** Run skill `verify-aura-ui` (`pnpm lint`) and clear findings on files you touched. 5. **Monorepo only.** Follow root `AGENTS.md`. At PR time, run skill `update-feature-map`. Do not write progress logs. ## Where to go next | Task | Open | | --- | --- | | Token narrative | `DESIGN.md` | | Monorepo scope, public APIs, stories | `AGENTS.md` | | CLI commands | [cli.md](./cli.md) | | Theming without new hex values | [customization.md](./customization.md) | | shadcn CLI, registries, presets | skill `shadcn` — Aura Keep still wins | | Forms end to end | skill `aura-forms` | | Port a component | skill `port-component-to-aura` | | Feature-map note | skill `update-feature-map` |

name: generate-brand-images
description: Generates identity-consistent Gemini images and integrates them into landing pages. Use when creating or redesigning a landing page, hero, marketing page, or visual asset set that may need generated imagery.
---

# Generate brand images

Generate image assets from the product identity in the blueprint Obsidian vault. The project only needs a Gemini API key in `.env`; the bundled script handles prompt assembly, batch generation, and file output.

## 1. Read identity before designing

1. Locate the vault at `wiki/obsidian-*/`.
2. Read the notes in `01-Identity/`, starting with `Image-Identity.md`.
3. Treat image identity as ready only when the notes define at least:
   - visual medium or photographic/illustration style;
   - palette and lighting;
   - composition or recurring motifs;
   - exclusions or brand constraints.

A scaffolded `Image-Identity.md` with `status: needs-definition`, placeholders, or generic product copy is not a defined image identity.

If image identity is not ready, stop before generating and ask focused questions about the missing dimensions. After the user answers, update `01-Identity/Image-Identity.md`, set `status: ready`, and continue.

## 2. Check image generation access

The script reads `.env` automatically and accepts either:

```dotenv
GOOGLE_API_KEY=
# or
GEMINI_API_KEY=
```

Never print, copy into markdown, or commit a real key.

If neither variable has a value, ask the user to choose:

1. add their Google AI Studio key to `.env`, then retry;
2. let the agent generate the images with its native image-generation capability, when available;
3. continue with deliberate placeholders.

Do not fabricate or attempt to provision a Google API key. If the user chooses the agent-native option, preserve the same identity, filenames, dimensions, and integration workflow.

## 3. Plan the landing asset set

Inspect the page structure before generating. Prefer the smallest useful set of images; do not add imagery to sections that are clearer with typography or UI.

Create `tmp/aura-image-plan.json`:

```json
{
  "identity": "wiki/obsidian-project/01-Identity/Image-Identity.md",
  "images": [
    {
      "prompt": "Wide hero scene with the primary subject weighted right and clean negative space left",
      "output": "public/generated/landing/hero",
      "aspectRatio": "16:9"
    },
    {
      "prompt": "Supporting editorial image for the benefits section",
      "output": "public/generated/landing/benefits",
      "aspectRatio": "4:5"
    }
  ]
}
```

Allowed aspect ratios are `1:1`, `2:3`, `3:2`, `3:4`, `4:3`, `4:5`, `5:4`, `9:16`, `16:9`, and `21:9`. Keep output paths inside the project. Describe composition, subject placement, crop safety, and whether negative space is needed; the script adds the identity and no-baked-text constraint.

## 4. Generate

Preview the resolved prompts without an API call:

```bash
pnpm ai:image -- --manifest tmp/aura-image-plan.json --dry-run
```

Generate the complete set:

```bash
pnpm ai:image -- --manifest tmp/aura-image-plan.json
```

For one image:

```bash
pnpm ai:image -- --identity wiki/obsidian-project/01-Identity/Image-Identity.md --prompt "Centered product still life" --output public/generated/product --aspect 1:1
```

The script uses `gemini-2.5-flash-image`, creates parent directories, and selects the extension from the returned MIME type. Read its `saved ...` lines before wiring paths into code.

## 5. Integrate and verify

- Use generated local assets through the framework image component when available.
- Write useful alt text from the image's purpose; use empty alt only for truly decorative images.
- Keep text, logos, and UI labels in HTML rather than baking them into generated pixels.
- Check desktop and mobile crops and preserve focal subjects.
- Run the project's relevant lint, typecheck, and build checks.
- Record the asset plan, accepted outputs, and implementation paths in the blueprint wiki. Never record the API key.

Generated images require human review. Regenerate outputs with accidental text, identity drift, unsafe crops, visual artifacts, or inaccessible contrast.

name: port-component-to-aura
description: >-
  Ports a UI component from a URL (shadcn, another registry, or design-system docs)
  into Aura-styled code. Detects two scenarios: (1) consumer app — write into the
  project's components; (2) aura-design-system monorepo — add to the registry with
  Ladle story + metadata for docs. Use when the user pastes ui.shadcn.com,
  auradesignsystem.com, a registry JSON URL, or asks to recreate/adapt a component in Aura.
---

# Port component to Aura

Recreate an external component with Aura tokens and primitives. Prefer Aura patterns; do not paste upstream class soup.

## Detect scenario first

| Signal | Scenario |
| --- | --- |
| Repo has `packages/registry/registry/default/components/` and `packages/registry/src/*.stories.tsx` (this monorepo / `aura-design-system`) | **A — Aura registry (document for the design system)** |
| Otherwise (app with `components.json`, `@aura` registry, typical Next app) | **B — Consumer project (for this app only)** |

If unclear, ask once: “¿Esto va al registry de Aura (Ladle + docs) o solo a este proyecto?”

Shared mapping rules apply in both scenarios. Deliverables differ.

## When to use

- User pastes a shadcn / registry / design-system docs URL
- User asks to recreate, adapt, or port a component “in Aura”
- User wants Aura-styled UI from an external example

## Shared: read source + map

### Read (do not install blindly)

| Source | How to load |
| --- | --- |
| shadcn / `@namespace/name` | shadcn MCP, or `https://ui.shadcn.com/r/{name}.json` |
| Aura | `@aura` / `@aura-dev`, or (in monorepo) `apps/www/public/r/{name}.json` |
| Other docs URL | Fetch; extract API, variants, a11y, structure |
| Non-registry DS | Fetch + interpret only |

### Map to Aura

- Reuse Aura primitives already in the target (`Button`, `Dialog`, `Input`, `class-names`, etc.)
- Icons: Lucide → `@radix-ui/react-icons` with `className="icon"`
- Spacing: `--spacing: 13px` (`p-4` = 52px)
- Typography: fluid `.h1`–`.p`; no `text-xl` for primary copy; `text-sm` / `text-xs` OK for utility **except** editable `input` / `textarea` / `select` (MUST stay ≥ 17px for iOS)
- Color: `--accent-*` / `--gray-*` steps 1–12; no one-off hex
- Motion: `transform` + `opacity`; honor `prefers-reduced-motion`
- Follow `DESIGN.md` and `.agents/skills/aura/`. After the port, run skill `verify-aura-ui`.

---

## Scenario B — Consumer project (for this app)

Goal: a component the **app can use**, not publish to Aura’s public registry.

### Do

1. Prefer installing an existing Aura item if it already covers the need: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @aura/<name>` (or MCP install).
2. If porting/adapting: write source into the app paths from `components.json` aliases (usually `@/components/ui`, `@/components`, `@/utils`).
3. Wire imports to local Aura utilities (`@/utils/class-names`, existing UI primitives).
4. Optionally add a small usage example in a page or demo the app already uses — **do not** invent Ladle/registry paths.

### Do not

- Create `packages/registry/...`, `*.stories.tsx` under a registry package, or `metadata/*.yml`
- Run `registry:generate` / `registry:build` / `docs:generate`
- Treat the result as a new `@aura/<name>` for others to install

### Done when

- [ ] Compiles in the app
- [ ] Uses Aura tokens / rules
- [ ] Fits existing app folder conventions
- [ ] Accessible enough for production use in that project

---

## Scenario A — Aura design system (document for the registry)

Goal: a **registry item** others install as `@aura/<kebab-name>`, with Ladle + docs automation.

### Required deliverables

| Artifact | Path | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Component | `packages/registry/registry/default/components/ui/{PascalName}.tsx` (or `components/` for non-ui peers) | Source of truth |
| Ladle story | `packages/registry/src/{kebab-name}.stories.tsx` | Storybook (Ladle) |
| Metadata | `packages/registry/metadata/{kebab-name}.yml` | `docs:generate` preview/usage |
| Built JSON | `apps/www/public/r/{kebab-name}.json` | `@aura/{kebab-name}` |

Non-UI peers (e.g. DataGrid) may live under `components/` instead of `ui/` — match peers.

### Do not

- `shadcn add` upstream shadcn into `packages/registry` — fetch and rewrite
- Skip story or metadata (docs preview depends on them)

### Write component

1. Source under `registry/default/components/ui/` (PascalCase, Aura patterns).
2. `pnpm registry:generate` in `packages/registry` refreshes `registry.json`.
3. Set npm / `@aura/...` dependencies as peers do.

### Ladle story (required)

`packages/registry/src/{kebab-name}.stories.tsx`:

- Import from `../registry/default/components/...` (not `@/` in stories).
- **Must `export const Default`** — metadata uses `preview: Default`; `generate-docs.ts` extracts it.
- Extra named stories → Usage section (`usage: all`).
- Must run in Ladle: `pnpm --filter @aura-design/registry dev`.

```tsx
import { Button } from "../registry/default/components/ui/Button";
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetTrigger,
  SheetContent,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetDescription,
} from "../registry/default/components/ui/Sheet";

export const Default = () => (
  <Sheet>
    <SheetTrigger asChild>
      <Button>Open sheet</Button>
    </SheetTrigger>
    <SheetContent>
      <SheetHeader>
        <SheetTitle>Sheet title</SheetTitle>
        <SheetDescription>Description.</SheetDescription>
      </SheetHeader>
    </SheetContent>
  </Sheet>
);
```

### Metadata YAML (required)

`packages/registry/metadata/{kebab-name}.yml`:

```yaml
header:
  description: One-line description of the component.
extends: _templates/content.yml
```

Template expands to `preview: Default`, `installation: @aura`, `source: all`, `usage: all`. Without YAML or `Default`, docs preview degrades.

### Build and verify

```bash
# from packages/registry
pnpm registry:generate
pnpm registry:build
pnpm docs:generate   # when MDX/demos should update
pnpm dev             # Ladle
```

Or `pnpm registry:bootstrap`.

### Done when

- [ ] `@aura/<kebab-name>` builds under `apps/www/public/r/`
- [ ] Story with **`export const Default`**
- [ ] `metadata/<kebab-name>.yml` present
- [ ] Ladle renders the story
- [ ] A11y + Aura tokens/rules; no class soup fighting the 13px grid

---

# Update feature map

Run once per PR, after the code is final. Guardrails live in `.agents/rules/feature-map.mdc`.

## Steps

1. Open `wiki/obsidian-*/Feature-Map/`. Find the note whose `feature` matches what the PR changes. Read that note only.
2. Update it, or create `Feature-Map/<Feature-Name>.md` with the shape below. One note per feature, not per PR.
3. Set `pr` to this PR's URL and `updated` to today. Fix `status`, `routes`, and `components` if they moved.
4. Keep the body to 2–4 sentences: what the feature does for the user and where it lives. No session log, no history.
5. Commit the note in the same PR. Do not edit `Feature-Map.base`.

## Note shape

```markdown
---
feature: Checkout
status: shipped
area: commerce
routes: [/checkout]
components: [app/checkout/page.tsx, components/checkout-form.tsx]
pr: https://github.com/org/repo/pull/123
updated: 2026-01-31
---
What it does for the user, in one or two sentences. Where the entry points live.
```

* `status`: `planned`, `in-progress`, `shipped`, or `deprecated`.
* `routes` and `components`: repo-relative paths or URL routes. Use `[]` when none apply.

## Done when

* [ ] Every feature the PR changes has a note with this PR in `pr`.
* [ ] No other wiki, progress, or assumptions file was read or written.

# Verify Aura UI

Guardrails live in `.agents/skills/aura/rules/lint.md` and the rest of `.agents/skills/aura/`. This skill is the verify/fix loop.

## After every UI change

1. Run `pnpm lint` (project script is `eslint`).
2. Filter for `@shadcn/lint` on files you touched:
   * `shadcn/no-restyle`
   * `shadcn/no-arbitrary-values`
   * `shadcn/no-raw-colors`
   * `aura/no-icon-margin`
3. Fix findings before finishing the task.
   * Restyle → use component variants/sizes, or layout/width only on the call site.
   * Arbitrary spacing → map to the 13px scale (`1` = 13px, `1.5` ≈ 19.5px, `2` = 26px).
   * Raw colors → `accent-*` / `gray-*` / semantic tokens from the theme.
   * Icon margin → drop horizontal margin; use container `gap-0.5` or rely on Button/Badge gap.
4. Re-run `pnpm lint` on the same scope. Treat new restyle/spacing **errors** as blockers. Pre-existing debt outside your files stays out of scope unless the human asks.

## Form control check

* Editable `input` / `textarea` / `select` must stay ≥ 17px. Do not add `text-sm` / `text-xs` on those controls.
* Prefer the global floor in `styles/main.css` / globals over per-call overrides.

## First-time install (only if missing)

Skip when `eslint.aura-shadcn.mjs` already exists and is merged into `eslint.config.mjs`.

1. Node ≥ 20.19, ESLint ≥ 9.30.
2. `pnpm add -D @shadcn/lint`
3. `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @aura/eslint-shadcn-lint`
4. Merge the exported config into `eslint.config.mjs` (see fragment header).
5. `settings.shadcn.ui` → `@/components/ui` (or the app alias).
6. Keep `no-restyle` / `no-arbitrary-values` **off** under `components/ui/**`.
7. Start severities at `warn`; promote to `error` as debt clears.
8. Point `settings.shadcn.note` at `DESIGN.md` and `.agents/skills/aura` when possible.

Upstream: [shadcn-ui/lint](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/lint).

## Done when

* [ ] `pnpm lint` has been run after the UI edit.
* [ ] No new `@shadcn/lint` restyle/spacing errors on touched files.
* [ ] Icon and 17px form floors still hold on the changed UI.
